The Driver

Jack
Haydu

Jack Haydu is an American open-wheel racing driver currently competing in both the F1600 and F2000 championships under the Formula Race Promotions (FRP) banner. Running two series simultaneously demands exceptional adaptability — and Jack is proving he has it.

Coming up through karting and into single-seater racing, Jack has built a foundation of technical racecraft, raw pace, and the mental discipline to compete consistently across multiple cars and categories in the same season. Every weekend is an opportunity to extract more data, more experience, and more speed.

The long-term target is USF Juniors — with a seat targeted for 2026 or the 2027 season at the latest. The work being done in FRP right now is a direct investment in earning that drive. Jack approaches racing as both a sport and a business, building the results, the media presence, and the sponsorship relationships needed to move up the ladder on his terms.

2026 Campaign

Two Series.
One Goal.

Jack is competing in both the FRP F1600 and FRP F2000 championships in 2026 — building mileage, racecraft, and results across two of America's most competitive junior single-seater categories.

F1600
FRP Series — Class 1
F1600
The FRP F1600 Championship is one of the most competitive entry-level single-seater series in North America. Built around the Van Diemen-style Formula Ford chassis powered by a 1600cc Duratec engine, F1600 is all about driver skill — no aero, no grip aids, no excuses. Pure racecraft in an equal-spec car where the driver makes the difference.
Engine Honda 1600cc
Configuration Open-Wheel Single-Seater
Format Equal-Spec — Driver-Dependent
Promoter Formula Race Promotions
F2000
FRP Series — Class 2
F2000
The FRP F2000 Championship steps it up with a more powerful and aerodynamically advanced single-seater, providing a closer approximation to the downforce and pace of higher-level open-wheel categories. Competing in F2000 alongside F1600 in the same season is a significant undertaking — and exactly the kind of aggressive development program needed to make the jump to USF Juniors.
Engine Ford 2000cc
Configuration Open-Wheel Single-Seater
Format Spec Series — FRP Sanctioned
Promoter Formula Race Promotions
Race Mentality

Eyes On
The Apex

Strapped in and locked in — this is where the work happens. Jack approaches every race weekend with a structured process: study data, learn the circuit, build confidence lap by lap, and push when the window is open.

Running both F1600 and F2000 in the same season means double the seat time, double the data, and twice the rate of development. That intensity is deliberate. USF Juniors demands drivers who are already operating at a high level — and 2026 is about proving that and earning that seat.

Racing Profile

How Jack Operates

From the cockpit to the content studio — Jack's program runs on multiple tracks simultaneously.

01
Seat Time
Double the Development
Racing both F1600 and F2000 in 2026 means more laps, more data, and faster development than a single-series campaign. Every race weekend produces twice the reference material.
02
Racecraft
Built on Equal-Spec Racing
F1600 in particular is a pure driver's series — no aero advantages, no setup tricks that mask talent. Pace in F1600 is real pace. It builds the racecraft that holds up at every level above it.
03
Data
Telemetry-Led Improvement
Every session is reviewed with telemetry — throttle traces, braking points, steering inputs, and lap-time breakdowns. The goal is not just to feel quick, but to understand exactly why and where.
04
Sim Racing
Year-Round Track Prep
High-fidelity sim racing keeps Jack sharp between events — allowing circuit preparation, setup analysis, and reaction training without the cost and logistics of on-track sessions.
05
Media
Built-In Audience
Over 80,000 combined followers and millions of monthly views across YouTube and social platforms. Sponsors get genuine audience access, not just a logo placement — Jack's content is the exposure vehicle.
06
Business
Professional from Day One
Jack treats racing like a business — building sponsor relationships, managing his brand, and approaching every partnership as a long-term, mutually beneficial arrangement rather than a one-off transaction.
Career Progression

The Road
to IndyCar

American open-wheel racing has one of the most structured career ladders in motorsport. Jack's program is built to climb it — step by step, season by season.

1
Karting
The foundation of every professional racing career. Jack spent years developing car control, racecraft, and competitive instincts in karting before making the transition into Formula cars.
Completed
2
FRP — F1600 and F2000
Currently competing in both the F1600 and F2000 championships under the Formula Race Promotions banner. Two series, twice the development. This is where the groundwork for USF Juniors gets laid — in data, mileage, and results.
Current — 2026
3
USF Juniors
Jack's primary target. The USF Juniors Championship is the official first step on the Road to IndyCar ladder. The target is a seat in 2026 — and if not this season, the 2027 campaign is the hard deadline. Everything in the current FRP program is building directly toward this.
Primary Target
4
USF 2000
The second step on the Road to IndyCar ladder. USF 2000 steps up the car specification and the level of competition, providing the bridge between junior open-wheel and the fully professional ranks. A direct progression from USF Juniors.
Future
5
USF Pro 2000
The third rung on the Road to IndyCar. USF Pro 2000 is a fully professional series with significant scholarship money on offer and direct visibility from IndyCar team management. Graduates of this series consistently move into Indy NXT.
Future
6
Indy NXT
One step from the top. Indy NXT is the premier proving ground for drivers knocking on the door of IndyCar — fully professional, nationally televised, and the final stop before the main series. The standard for the best young American open-wheel talent.
Future
7
IndyCar Series
The pinnacle of American open-wheel racing. The Indianapolis 500. The NTT IndyCar Series. The destination that shapes every decision Jack makes in 2026 and beyond — and the reason none of this is taken lightly.
Long-Term Target
